items.title: Margot Robbie Set to Star in A24's 'The Week of Pain'
items.summary:
Summary 

Margot Robbie will star in the upcoming film 'The Week of Pain' directed by Kristoffer BorgliA24 will finance and produce the project alongside Square Peg, Dilemma Films, and Robbie's LuckyChapThe announcement follows Borgli's recent box office success with The Drama starring Robert Pattinson and Zendaya

A24 is teaming up with director Kristoffer Borgli and actress Margot Robbie for an upcoming feature film titled The Week of Pain . Set to be financed and produced by A24, the project will also feature production contributions from Ari Aster and Lars Knudsen’s Square Peg banner, alongside Dilemma Films and Robbie’s own LuckyChap production company.

While official plot details for The Week of Pain remain heavily under wraps, the film is expected to deliver the squirmy, cringe-comedy drama that has become Borgli's signature following works like Dream Scenario and Sick of Myself . The new project reunites Square Peg and A24 with the filmmaker following their collaboration on April’s The Drama . That original dramedy, which starred Robert Pattinson and Zendaya, proved to be a massive box office success, grossing $135 million USD globally against a slim $28 million USD budget.

For Robbie, the casting announcement follows her recent appearance in the Warner Bros. cinematic adaptation of the literary romance Wuthering Heights . Starring alongside Jacob Elordi as Heathcliff, the film rocketed to $241 million USD worldwide. Looking ahead, the superstar is also set to star alongside Bradley Cooper in a highly anticipated Ocean’s 11 prequel centered around an epic heist…
items.t: Margot Robbie Set to Star in A24's 'The Week of Pain'

items.title: Jyodan and Amiide on Turning Noriko Kose’s “Still I Miss You” Into an Award-Winning Sampling Contest Track
items.summary:
Noriko Kose's "I Miss You" — a masterpiece famously sampled in Nujabes' iconic "Reflection Eternal" and cherished globally as part of the DNA of lo-fi and jazzy hip-hop — has been breathed new life. Released in October 2025, "Still I Miss You" is a piano instrumental created by Kose as a self-homage to that very song.

Using this track as their sampling source, Jyodan and Amiide took the grand prize in an official sampling contest co-hosted by Tribe (a sub-label of Hydeout Productions), SURF Music, and Hypebeast. Longtime collaborators who previously gained a core following as members of the hip-hop crew CIRRRCLE and who now operate out of Hawaii and London/Tokyo as solo artists and as the duo Otomodatchi, the pair crafted the track "but, I still miss U" out of respect for the original. While preserving Kose's beautiful piano melody, they elevated it into a new classic that bridges past, present, and future.

They discussed the story behind their winning track, their musical backgrounds, their current cross-border creative resonance,…

Buffer has released a Sony -inspired capsule led by the MDR-CD900ST Buffer SP, its version of the Japanese studio headphone, alongside three graphic T-shirts based on Sony gear. The release celebrates the tools behind making and listening to music and video, from the recording booth to the skate video.

Specs follow the studio original: 63 Ω impedance, a 1,000 mW maximum input, a 5 to 30,000 Hz frequency response and a 2.5 m cable ending in a 6.3 mm stereo plug, with a 3.5 mm mini plug adapter included. The Sony headphones weigh about 200 g without the cable and are made in Japan, and they ship with a natural wood block.

Its back shows a wall of nine screens playing weather-forecast and news-style images next to “Buffy” and “Buffer” lettering, while a single monitor showing Buffy sits small on the chest. mineSEGA and Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio (RGG) have released the second story trailer for Stranger Than Heaven , moving Makoto Daito’s saga from Kokura in 1915 to Kure, Hiroshima, in 1929. From there, his new role takes shape: he oversees the city’s gambling halls and collects debts owed to the clan. The trailer intercuts his rise with combat as he earns the nickname “Red Oni.” SEGA’s official description frames the act bluntly: “In Kure, Daito swears his loyalty to Iwaki Genzo, and steels himself to commit any atrocities to climb the yakuza ranks.” The trailer also hints at the cost, showing Daito struggling with his life in the yakuza and facing the choices that led him there.

Previously codenamed “Project Century,” Stranger Than Heaven is RGG Studio’s latest project after its long-running Yakuza/Like a Dragon series. The game follows Daito across five eras and five cities between 1915 and 1965. Its settings include Kokura, Fukuoka; Kure; Minami, Osaka; Atami, Shizuoka; and Kamurocho, the fictional Tokyo district that anchors the…

Scheduled to launch in the back half of the 2020s, the Slate Truck lacks a central screen and digital bloat, embracing a minimalist design language. Drivers navigate a cabin featuring manual hand-crank windows and no traditional carpeting. Slate built the vehicle with the expectation that owners will mount their own smartphones to handle navigation and entertainment needs.

The "Screenless GPS" highlights the automaker's back-to-basics design, offering a physical map instead of a glowing central infotainment hub. items.title: Netflix’s 'Magic: The Gathering' Animated Series, 'Planeswalker,' Is Officially Coming in 2027

Summary 

Netflix drops a sneak peek for the reworked animated series debuting in 2027Roy Graham confirms the highly anticipated adaptation is officially titled PlaneswalkerThe release puts an end to a chaotic seven-year development cycle following a ground-up rework

After years of false starts and behind-the-scenes silence, the multiverse is finally opening up. Netflix dropped a sneak peek video officially announcing that the long-awaited animated adaptation of the iconic card game is set to debut in 2027. Officially titled Magic The Gathering : Planeswalker , the series arrives with a heavy burden of expectation, prompting the franchise’s brass to address the fanbase directly. Roy Graham, the Head of Story at Magic: The Gathering , introduced the teaser video with a mix of relief and reassurance, stating, "It’s really happening. I promise. For real." That self-aware introduction directly addresses the heavy skepticism surrounding a project that has been largely theoretical for the better part of a decade.

The 2027 debut of Planeswalker resolves an exhausting seven-year development cycle that saw the property pushed to the brink of cancellation. An animated Magic: The Gathering series was first teased in 2019. That original version was initially helmed by Joe and Anthony Russo, carrying heavy prestige before the highly publicized project fell apart. For years, the property sat in limbo until Netflix confirmed in 2024 that it still planned to adapt the game, though the streaming giant mandated reworking the series entirely from the ground up. items.title: Sony Patents a PlayStation Controller That Lets You Tap a Card or Phone to Pay for Games
items.summary:
Summary 

Sony filed a 2025 provisional patent for a controller feature that pulls payment and login data from nearby smart devices or cards via proximity sensorsThe single-tap action is designed to eliminate manual typing, reducing cart abandonment on the digital storefront while streamlining player loginsA frictionless checkout process is increasingly critical to the ecosystem as Sony prepares to discontinue physical disc production by 2028

Sony aims to eliminate the friction of typing out credit card numbers with an analog stick. In a 2025 provisional patent titled " Video game controller-driven information transfer, " the gaming giant outlined a PlayStation controller built with integrated proximity detection. The hardware receives payment details or account information directly from a nearby smartphone or physical card, seamlessly passing that data to the console. The controller relies on near-field communication (NFC), a Bluetooth connection or a combination of both to detect a nearby device, receive its signal and secure confirmation before transmitting the data to the console.

These information transfers trigger automatically in response to what the filing defines as "an event that has occurred at the video game console." According to the patent’s internal diagrams, console events that prompt a data transfer include purchasing a PlayStation game, entering gift card details or joining a multiplayer match. Users can complete these traditionally tedious actions with a single tap of their device. The inventors purpose-built this method to bypass digging through a…
items.t: Sony Patents a PlayStation Controller That Lets You Tap a Card or Phone to Pay for Games

Professional golfer Bryson DeChambeau has officially unveiled plans for The Orchard Golf Club, marking the two-time U.S. Open champion's first foray into golf course design. Teaming up with real estate developer Cook Land Company, the athlete aims to build an 18-hole championship course and a sprawling residential community in his hometown of Clovis, California . The "mega" project is set to be developed on the historic McFarlane Ranch, a site that has operated for three generations cultivating crops like citrus and almonds.

Driven by a desire to give back to the region where he grew up and attended Clovis East High School, DeChambeau envisions the project as a community-oriented destination. In a distinct nod to the Central Valley’s rich agricultural roots, the proposed course design will feature a different variety of fruit or nut tree surrounding each of the 18 holes. The massive development is projected to bring significant growth to the area, with DeChambeau estimating it could increase the city's 120,000-resident population by up to 30 percent.

Apple is already looking ahead to its next major hardware evolution, preparing to introduce the second-generation iPhone Duo 2 next fall. While the standard array of chip upgrades and baseline camera improvements are expected, the tech giant is setting its sights on more ambitious overhauls to refine its dual-screen flagship. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman , Apple currently holds two major development priorities for the upcoming device: integrating Face ID and reimagining the Action Button.

The push for advanced biometrics marks a shift in how Apple views its foldable user experience, making Face ID integration a top priority for upcoming generations. Apple engineers have already developed working prototypes of the iPhone Duo 2 equipped with Face ID, actively working to integrate the facial-recognition system specifically into the device's outer display . Placing the sensor on the cover screen allows users to authenticate without opening the handset.

items.title: Portugal Immortalizes Cristiano Ronaldo's Legacy With a New No. 7 Jersey Design
items.summary:
Summary 

The Portugal Football Association has announced a graphic design update to its No. 7 jersey to honor Cristiano RonaldoBecause FIFA regulations prevent the outright retirement of the number, the new design features a small cross on the digitThe updated jersey will debut during the team's upcoming Nations League match against Denmark following Ronaldo's recent retirement

The Portugal Football Association has officially announced a design update to its iconic No. 7 jersey, serving as a permanent tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo 's storied international career. Debuting during the team's upcoming Nations League match against Denmark, the design shift marks Portugal's first game since the 41-year-old forward announced his retirement from the national team earlier this month.

Concluding his international run with a staggering 146 goals across 234 matches, Ronaldo stepped away from the squad on November 5 following a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus. Because strict FIFA stipulations prevent national federations from officially retiring jersey numbers, the governing body opted for a visual workaround to honor the athlete's legacy. The newly updated No. 7 kit features a modified graphic design that incorporates a small cross on the digit, symbolically drawing a line after Ronaldo's historic era.

items.title: JW Anderson and Johnstons of Elgin Reimagine Archival Checks in New Coats and Knits
items.summary:
JW Anderson and historic luxury textile brand Johnstons of Elgin , hailing from northeastern Scotland, have unveiled a new Scottish-made capsule collection.

Rooted in an archival check pattern from Johnstons of Elgin, this collaboration fuses the distinct craftsmanship and design aesthetics both brands have cultivated over the years. The three-piece lineup features a coat, a sweater, and a scarf. Entirely produced in Scotland, the pieces combine traditional textile techniques with JW Anderson's signature graphic edge.

Crafted from the same raw materials as the knitwear, the coat renders a boldly oversized check pattern in a thick, substantial weave. Cut in a double-breasted silhouette, it features fringed edges that push the rich texture of the textile to the forefront.

The sweater reconstructs the coat's striking red check into a three-dimensional jacquard knit. By knitting the pattern on both the front and the back, the piece achieves a beautifully textured finish distinct from woven fabrics. The entire process, from knitting to the final touches, takes place at the Johnstons of Elgin mill in Hawick, a town in the Scottish Borders renowned for its cashmere production.

The scarf incorporates curated motifs from both brands' archives and current collections. It pairs a lamb illustration from a 1930s Johnstons of Elgin archive with the Ribbon Anchor that JW Anderson debuted in its Resort/Spring 2026 collection, seamlessly bringing together creative elements from different eras into a single, cohesive design.

The collection is slated for release at JW Anderson and…

items.summary:
Whether you want minimalist or heritage, waterproof or suede, our menswear expert has rounded up the most stylish pairs for every occasion and outfit

• The best men’s coats for autumn and winter

I haven’t always worn boots. For years I wrote them off – at 5ft 8in, I was convinced anything above the ankle would make my legs look shorter. Then I started wearing them with the right trousers – a straight leg that falls over the top – and realised I’d spent a decade getting winter wrong. All anyone sees is a smart pair of shoes that happens to keep your ankles warm.

Here’s the thing: boots needn’t be intimidating. They’re just the wintry version of the leather shoes you already own. A chelsea is your loafer – it goes with pretty much everything in your wardrobe and every event in your diary, Christmas parties included. A derby boot is laced up, a bit sturdier and just as happy with jeans. The chukka is your weekend trainer. And the chunky, rubber-soled ones? Just think of them as an umbrella for your feet.

items.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: this season’s big idea? Wear a skirt. It’s that simple
items.summary:
All you need to look on-trend this autumn is a skirt, but instead of going shopping, check what you already have in your wardrobe

I go to a lot of fashion shows, and sometimes they are gorgeous and sometimes they are ugly. Sometimes they are electrifying and sometimes they are deathly dull. Sometimes they are completely baffling. My absolute favourite kind of show is the one that makes me want to run home and change my outfit. A show that makes me think: there it is! That’s exactly what I want to wear. When the look speaks to me, as if it had been on the tip of my tongue. God, I love that.

Which is what happened at Prada this season. The idea was: skirts. That’s it, that’s the whole idea. The show was 63 different skirts – some with a sweater, some with a bra top, some with a jacket, but the point was the skirts. They were knee-length, give or take an inch up or down, and A-line, although sometimes a narrow almost-pencil and other times with a broader flare. There were skirts that wrapped like kilts, held together with strips of industrial-weight Velcro embroidered with tiny gems. There were stiff boxy pleated skirts and tube skirts painted with swirls, and dainty embellished skirts with a layer of gauze on top, like a petticoat worn on the outside.

Continue reading...
items.t: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: this season’s big idea? Wear a skirt. It’s that simple
